quiz.about: NCERT Class 12 Maths, Determinants Exercise 4.6 — solving systems using matrices

questions.q: For the matrix equation AX = B, when is the unique-solution formula X = A⁻¹B valid?
questions.explanation: A⁻¹ exists only when A is non-singular, that is |A| ≠ 0. Then X = A⁻¹B gives the unique solution.

questions.q: A system AX = B with |A| ≠ 0 is called:
questions.explanation: |A| ≠ 0 means A is invertible, so the system is consistent and has exactly one solution.

questions.q: If |A| = 0 and (adj A) B ≠ 0, the system AX = B is:
questions.explanation: When |A| = 0 and (adj A)B ≠ 0 the equations contradict each other, so no solution exists — the system is inconsistent.

questions.q: If |A| = 0 and (adj A) B = 0, the system AX = B usually has:
questions.explanation: With |A| = 0 and (adj A)B = 0 the system, if consistent, has infinitely many solutions.

questions.q: For the system 2x + 5y = 1, 3x + 2y = 7, the value of |A| is:
questions.explanation: |A| = (2)(2) − (5)(3) = 4 − 15 = −11. Since it is non-zero, the system has a unique solution.

faq.q: What does Exercise 4.6 of Class 12 Determinants cover?
faq.a: It focuses on solving systems of linear equations using matrices — writing the system as AX = B, finding A⁻¹, and applying X = A⁻¹B. It also covers checking whether a system is consistent or inconsistent.

faq.q: How do I know if a system of equations is consistent?
faq.a: Compute |A|. If |A| ≠ 0 the system is consistent with a unique solution. If |A| = 0, check (adj A)B: if it is zero the system may have infinitely many solutions, and if it is non-zero the system is inconsistent with no solution.

faq.q: When can I use X = A⁻¹B to solve a system?
faq.a: Only when the coefficient matrix A is square and non-singular, that is |A| ≠ 0, so that A⁻¹ exists. If |A| = 0 the inverse method does not apply and you analyse consistency separately.

faq.q: What is the difference between a unique solution and infinitely many solutions?
faq.a: A unique solution occurs when |A| ≠ 0 — the lines or planes meet at a single point. Infinitely many solutions occur when |A| = 0 and the equations are dependent yet consistent, so the whole solution set satisfies them.
